frameworks.name: CIS Critical Security Controls v8
frameworks.note: References are to CIS Controls v8 safeguard numbers. This project does not reproduce the text of any CIS Benchmark, which is separately licensed.

frameworks.name: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5
frameworks.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
frameworks.note: References are to control identifiers in the SP 800-53 Rev. 5 catalogue.

frameworks.name: DISA Network Device Management SRG
frameworks.note: References name the applicable requirement family rather than a version-specific V-ID, because STIG rule identifiers change with each benchmark release.

frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A
frameworks.note: References are to Annex A control numbers in the 2022 revision.

rules.title: Telnet management access must be disabled
rules.description: No administrative interface on the device may accept Telnet connections.
rules.impact: Telnet carries the session, including administrative credentials, as cleartext. Anyone able to observe traffic on any intermediate link can recover the password and take full control of the device.

STIG: Management traffic must be transmitted over an approved encrypted path

rules.title: Default SNMP community strings must not be used
rules.description: Community strings such as 'public' or 'private' must be removed.
rules.impact: Default community strings are published in every vendor manual and are the first thing an attacker tries. A readable community exposes the full device configuration; a writable one permits reconfiguration.

STIG: Default authenticators must be changed before deployment

rules.title: SSH must be restricted to protocol version 2
rules.description: The SSH server must not accept SSH protocol version 1.
rules.impact: SSHv1 has structural weaknesses in its integrity checking that permit session tampering, and is deprecated by every current standard.

STIG: Deprecated cryptographic protocol versions must be disabled

rules.title: Plaintext HTTP management must be disabled
rules.description: The unencrypted web administration server must not be running.
rules.impact: The HTTP management interface transmits session cookies and credentials without encryption, and widens the device's attack surface with a full web stack.

STIG: Non-essential and unencrypted services must be disabled

rules.title: SNMP v1/v2c must be disabled
rules.description: Community-string based SNMP must be replaced by SNMPv3.
rules.impact: SNMP v1 and v2c authenticate with a cleartext community string and provide no message integrity, so both the credential and the returned configuration data are exposed on the wire.

STIG: Unauthenticated management protocols must be disabled

rules.title: Privileged mode must be protected by a hashed secret
rules.description: Privilege escalation must require a strongly hashed secret rather than a reversible password.
rules.impact: Reversible privileged passwords can be decoded offline from a captured configuration file, turning read access to a backup into full administrative control.

STIG: Privileged access must require strong authentication

rules.title: Stored passwords must not be readable in the configuration
rules.description: Password encryption must be enabled so credentials are not written in cleartext.
rules.impact: Configuration files are routinely copied to backup servers, ticketing systems and version control. Cleartext credentials in those files spread far beyond the device.

STIG: Stored authenticators must be cryptographically protected

rules.title: Well-known default accounts must be removed
rules.description: Accounts using predictable names such as admin, cisco or root must not exist.
rules.impact: A known account name removes half of the work in a credential attack and is the standard target of automated scanning against management interfaces.

STIG: Default accounts must be removed, disabled or renamed

rules.title: Logs must be forwarded to a remote collector
rules.description: At least one external syslog destination must be configured.
rules.impact: Local logs are held in volatile memory and are lost on reboot. They are also the first thing an intruder clears, so without off-box copies an incident leaves no evidence.

STIG: Audit records must be offloaded to a central repository

rules.title: Management access must be restricted to trusted sources
rules.description: An access list or trusted-host list must limit which sources may open an administrative session.
rules.impact: Without a source restriction the management plane is reachable from any host that can route to the device, so a single compromised workstation anywhere on the network can reach it.

STIG: Management access must be restricted to designated management networks

rules.title: SSH must use strong ciphers and key exchange
rules.description: Weak SSH ciphers such as 3DES and CBC-mode algorithms must be explicitly disabled.
rules.impact: Legacy cipher suites remain negotiable unless explicitly removed, allowing a downgrade to algorithms with known weaknesses.

STIG: Only approved cryptographic algorithms may be used

rules.title: A minimum password length must be enforced
rules.description: Locally defined accounts must require a password of at least 12 characters.
rules.impact: Short passwords fall quickly to offline cracking once a configuration file or hash is obtained.

STIG: Password length requirements must be enforced

rules.title: Centralised AAA should be configured
rules.description: Authentication should be delegated to a central TACACS+ or RADIUS service.
rules.impact: Local-only accounts cannot be revoked centrally, so an administrator who leaves the organisation retains access to every device provisioned with a local credential.

STIG: Devices must use a centralised authentication service

rules.title: Local logging must be enabled
rules.description: The device must retain log messages locally.
rules.impact: Without local logging there is no record available during an outage that severs connectivity to the central collector.

STIG: The device must generate audit records

rules.title: Administrative actions must be logged
rules.description: Configuration changes and administrative commands must be recorded.
rules.impact: Without command accounting there is no attribution for a change, so an unauthorised modification cannot be distinguished from routine maintenance.

STIG: Audit records must capture privileged command execution

rules.title: A time source must be configured
rules.description: The device must synchronise its clock with at least one NTP server.
rules.impact: Log entries from a device with an unsynchronised clock cannot be correlated with other systems, which makes incident reconstruction and legal evidence unreliable.

STIG: System clocks must be synchronised to an authoritative time source

rules.title: Idle administrative sessions must time out
rules.description: An idle management session must be closed within ten minutes.
rules.impact: An unattended session on an authenticated terminal grants full device control to anyone with physical access to that terminal.

STIG: Sessions must be terminated after a defined period of inactivity

rules.title: IP source routing must be disabled
rules.description: The device must not honour source-routed packets.
rules.impact: Source routing lets a sender dictate the path a packet takes, which can be used to bypass filtering and reach networks that routing policy would otherwise protect.

STIG: Non-essential IP options must be disabled

rules.title: Legacy small servers must be disabled
rules.description: Echo, chargen and discard services must not be running.
rules.impact: These diagnostic services have no operational purpose on a production network and are readily abused as traffic amplifiers in denial-of-service attacks.

STIG: Non-essential services must be disabled

rules.title: SSH must be available for management
rules.description: An encrypted administrative transport must be available.
rules.impact: If no encrypted transport is offered, administrators are pushed onto cleartext alternatives or onto console access that cannot be centrally audited.

STIG: Management sessions must use an approved encrypted protocol

rules.title: HTTPS should be used where web management is required
rules.description: If a web administration interface is needed, it must be the encrypted one.
rules.impact: This control is only meaningful alongside the requirement to disable plaintext HTTP; on its own an enabled HTTPS service still widens the attack surface.

STIG: Web-based management must use TLS

rules.title: NTP peers should be authenticated
rules.description: NTP associations should be cryptographically authenticated.
rules.impact: An unauthenticated time source can be spoofed to shift the device clock, which corrupts log ordering and can bring expired certificates back into validity.

STIG: Time sources must be authenticated

rules.title: A legal login banner must be displayed
rules.description: A warning notice must be presented before authentication.
rules.impact: Many jurisdictions require an explicit notice that access is restricted and monitored before unauthorised use can be prosecuted.

STIG: A DoD-approved notice and consent banner must be displayed
